territory: volatility-ETP term structure, roll yield and short-vol carry

bootstrap_null.statistic: max over formulas of AS-WRITTEN net-of-cost Sharpe (signs fixed a priori)

results.name: D2_VIX_MA_GATE
results.why: Long SVXY only while VIX is below its own 50d average: vol is a regime variable and the roll is only reliably paid inside the calm regime.

results.name: B2_ETP_LADDER_CARRY_21
results.why: Same tradable roll estimator over 21 days: a faster read of whether the front bucket is currently the one being bled by the roll.

results.name: B6_REALISED_DECAY
results.why: Long SVXY when the front ETP has been decaying over the last 21 days: the ETP's own realised drift is the most direct evidence that the forced roll is currently a cost.

results.name: Z1_STATIC_SHORT_VIXY
results.why: BENCHMARK: the same short-vol exposure expressed by borrowing the long-vol ETP, so the 5%/yr borrow line is visible next to the borrow-free SVXY version.

results.name: G3_MID_BUCKET_CARRY
results.why: Long VIXM-short-side via a short VIXM position in contango: the mid bucket also pays a roll, smaller but far less convex, so it is the low-tail version of the same trade.

results.name: G1_VVIX_SCALED_CARRY
results.why: Long SVXY in contango, sized inversely to z252 of VVIX: the price of VIX convexity is the market's own quote for the risk this book is short.

results.name: A1_CONTANGO_SIGN_3M
results.why: Long SVXY only while log(VIX3M/VIX)>0: the forced daily front->second roll is a loss for the long-vol holder exactly when the 30d->93d curve slopes up.

results.name: A4_NEARSLOPE_SIGN
results.why: Long SVXY only while log(VIX/VIX9D)>0: the 9d->30d segment inverts FIRST in a vol shock, so it is the earliest free read that the forced roll has flipped.

results.name: D4_INVERSION_KILL
results.why: Long SVXY unless the 9d->30d segment has inverted: the near segment inverts first, so it is the cheapest available kill switch on the forced roll flipping sign.

results.name: A7_SLOPE_MOMENTUM
results.why: Long SVXY when the 30d->93d slope has STEEPENED over 5 days: the forced roll cost the long-vol ETP pays is re-set daily, so a steepening curve raises tomorrow's carry.

results.name: D8_EQUITY_HEDGED_CARRY
results.why: Long SVXY, short 0.35 SPY: strip the equity beta so what is left is the roll and the variance premium rather than a leveraged bet that stocks go up.

results.name: C5_VRP_AND_CONTANGO
results.why: Long SVXY only when the premium exists AND the curve slopes up: the premium is the cause, the slope is the transmission; require both links of the chain.

results.name: B4_CAL_SPREAD_STATIC
results.why: Always long VIXM / short VIXY, gross 1: a pure maturity spread on one curve. The front bucket rolls a bigger fraction of its book per day than the mid bucket, so the spread harvests the roll differential with no outright vol direction.

results.name: F1_LAST_WEEK_OF_CYCLE
results.why: Long SVXY only in the last 5 sessions before VIX settlement (and only in contango): front-contract convergence per day is (F1-spot)/dte, which is largest as dte shrinks.

results.name: A8_DUAL_GATE
results.why: Long SVXY only when BOTH the 9d->30d and 30d->93d segments slope up: require the whole front of the curve to be paying the roll, not just one segment.

results.name: A9_TRIPLE_GATE
results.why: Long SVXY only when all three measured segments (9->30, 30->93, 93->186) slope up: the strictest possible statement that the entire term structure is in contango.

results.name: A6_BACKSLOPE
results.why: Long SVXY while the 93d->186d segment slopes up: the back end is where the pure term premium lives, unpolluted by short-dated event demand.

results.name: Z0_STATIC_LONG_SVXY
results.why: BENCHMARK, not a formula: hold the inverse short-term VIX-futures ETP always. Every gated formula below is a subset of this position, so this is the bar.

results.name: A3_CONTANGO_STEEP_ONLY
results.why: Long SVXY only when the 30d->93d slope is above its own trailing 252d median: shallow contango does not pay enough roll to cover the crash tail.

results.name: D7_BARBELL_TIMED
results.why: The barbell, with the SVXY sleeve gated on contango and the VIXM tail sleeve always on: the hedge must not be switched off by the same signal that sizes the risk.

results.name: B1_ETP_LADDER_CARRY_63
results.why: Long SVXY when 63d mean of (VIXM - VIXY) log returns is positive: the short bucket decaying faster than the mid bucket IS the realised front roll, priced in tradables.

results.name: F3_DTE_SCALED
results.why: Long SVXY in contango with size proportional to 1/sqrt(days to settlement): a smooth version of the convergence-acceleration claim rather than a hard calendar window.

results.name: C1_VRP_SIGN
results.why: Long SVXY when 30d implied vol exceeds SPY's trailing 21d realised vol: the option seller's premium is the source of the whole roll, so harvest it only when it exists.

results.name: B3_ETP_LADDER_Z
results.why: Size the SVXY carry by z504 of the tradable 63d roll estimator, long-only side.

results.name: D5_SPIKE_COOLDOWN
results.why: Long SVXY, but flat for 10 sessions after any 5-day +20% move in the front ETP: vol shocks cluster, and the second leg down is what killed the 2018 short-vol complex.

results.name: D6_BARBELL
results.why: Always 0.7 SVXY + 0.3 VIXM: pay part of the harvested roll back as permanent long convexity in the mid-term bucket, which does not gap the way the front does.

results.name: A5_CURVE_CONVEXITY
results.why: Long SVXY when the far slope exceeds the near slope (convex curve): a curve that is steep out front but flat behind is a stressed curve, and the roll is not safe.

results.name: E3_TWO_SIDED_SWITCH
results.why: Long SVXY in contango, long VIXY in backwardation: trade the SIGN of the mandated roll rather than only its profitable side; always invested, never flat.

results.name: C4_VRP_9D
results.why: Long SVXY when 9-day implied exceeds SPY's 5-day realised: the near-dated premium is where event-hedging demand concentrates and where the roll bites hardest.

results.name: G2_VIXY_REALVOL_SCALED
results.why: Long SVXY in contango, sized inversely to the front ETP's own 21d realised vol: a plain risk-parity sizing of the same carry, using tradable prices only.

results.name: F2_FIRST_HALF_OF_CYCLE
results.why: The complement: long SVXY only when more than 10 sessions remain to settlement. If F1 beats it, the convergence-acceleration story is wrong.

results.name: B5_CAL_SPREAD_TIMED
results.why: The same VIXM/VIXY maturity spread, on only while the 30d->93d curve slopes up: the roll differential reverses sign when the curve inverts.

results.name: D1_VIX_LEVEL_GATE
results.why: Long SVXY only while VIX closed under 20: above that, the crash convexity of a short vol-futures book dominates any roll it can collect.

results.name: B7_CALM_FRONT
results.why: Long SVXY when the front ETP's own 21d realised vol is below its 252d median: the roll is collected smoothly only when the front contract is not being repriced.

results.name: C3_VRP_RATIO_110
results.why: Long SVXY only when implied/realised exceeds 1.10: require the premium to be a clear margin, not a rounding difference between two noisy vol estimates.

results.name: A2_CONTANGO_Z
results.why: Size the SVXY carry by z252 of the 30d->93d slope: the roll paid per day is proportional to how steep the curve is, not merely to its sign.

results.name: D3_VVIX_GATE
results.why: Long SVXY only when VVIX/VIX is below its 252d median: a high vol-of-vol says the market is paying up for VIX convexity, which is precisely the risk being sold here.

results.name: E4_TWO_SIDED_LADDER
results.why: The same switch driven by the tradable VIXM-minus-VIXY roll estimator instead of the non-tradable VIX index curve.

results.name: C2_VRP_Z
results.why: Size the SVXY carry by z252 of the implied-minus-realised spread.

results.name: B8_LEVERAGE_DRAG_PAIR
results.why: Long VIXY 2 / short UVXY 1 (gross 1): the levered ETP must rebalance to target every close, so it compounds at minus half its variance relative to twice the 1x. That drag is mechanical and is collected without taking a view on the curve.

results.name: B9_LEVERAGE_DRAG_TIMED
results.why: The same levered-pair drag, sized by the measured 63d drag itself, on only when the drag has actually been negative (i.e. the rebalance is currently costing UVXY).
